query: I'm about to finish high school. Should I take a gap year before starting university?
atoms: perspective: Student with structured plan for gap year
perspective: Student uncertain about major or career direction
plausible_answers: Answer A (Gap Year if Structured Default): Take a gap year if you have a clear plan — structured gap years (work abroad, volunteering, skill building) produce higher GPA and major satisfaction, and most universities support deferral.

Answer B (Start University Immediately): Go straight to university if you don't have a specific gap year purpose — unstructured gap years rarely produce meaningful growth and risk undermining academic momentum without a clear plan.

Answer C (Gap Year for Career Clarity): Take a gap year specifically to explore different career environments if you're undecided about your major — a year of deliberate career testing before committing to a program reduces costly mid-degree changes.
baseline_answer: Answer A (Gap Year if Structured Default): Take a gap year if you have a clear plan — structured gap years (work abroad, volunteering, skill building) produce higher GPA and major satisfaction, and most universities support deferral.
